findings.title: Keep all new kernel FP work inside the saved canonical scope
findings.evidence: Update copies input floats to outputs before fp_save. Both functions restore via fp_leave before isfinite checks; init also compares work.life<0 after restore, and both publish float assignments afterward. Float loads/comparisons/stores can alter caller x87/MXCSR state or trap on denormal/signalling-NaN paths and occur under caller modes. This contradicts the full-state boundary; no measured failure on every platform is asserted.
findings.required_change: Use integer-bit ingress/egress; perform float loading, math and validation inside the canonical guard; settle results before restore/readback and publish by integer memcpy only. Preserve full-state matrix masks/seeds/oracles across normal, refusal, NeedPlaying and subnormal cases.

Scripted boot omits these calls. Changed-update additionally checks only3calls/0kills, not the actual per-call lifetime words it returned, so it proves at most a kill-decision change.

Model boot init in finite guards; never fake case6 failure for boot. Reconcile actual cohort lifetime words with sent answers when claiming aging authority, or explicitly narrow the verdict. Preserve delegated grammar/output checks, exact stop markers and genuine old-native capability red; no trace framework.
